summary.text: A son of Talaus in Apollodorus' Biantid roll and, in the usual genealogy, father of Hippomedon among the Seven against Thebes — though the same author records a rival claim that Hippomedon was Talaus' son directly.
Not to be confused with Aristomachus the Heraclid who helped lead the return to the Peloponnese.

story.text: Apollodorus names Aristomachus among the sons of Talaus and Lysimache, in the same Biantid catalogue that lists Adrastus, Pronax, Mecisteus, and Eriphyle. In the usual reckoning he is the father of Hippomedon, one of the Seven against Thebes.
